sentences.text: Abdounia was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes sharks and rays.
This genus belongs to the family Carcharhinidae, a group of modern sharks.
In the lower Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia, Abdounia teeth are the most common fossil shark teeth found there.
The genus Abdounia was formally described by Cappetta in 1980.
By the end of the Oligocene, the genus was severely reduced, likely due to competition with other sharks like Carcharhinus.
Abdounia lived between 66 and 27.3 million years ago.
Its fossils date from the Danian to the Rupelian stages.
Remains have been found in the Paleogene of Morocco, France, Belgium, Russia, and the United States.
